rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.

'Approval inflation' as a named failure mode is deliberately absent from the body (maintainer l.76), deferred to the exercise retro where it's earned.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity — consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, and mood-doesn't-resolve-early into one verdict.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Front-run check: strategy doc M2-detail (l.302) states the walk-down move is inlined as a plain prompt 'so M2 doesn't front-run M3's first-Skill-use moment' — this lecture and its maintainer block (l.74) confirm the skill reveal stays withheld. Module-to-module (intra-module) arc: close ('Making the plan good IS the work... the execution can wait for the day the task is real,' l.58-60) hands off cleanly to the 'Push back on the plan' exercise, which reuses this lecture's exact vocabulary as its own Phase 1-2 language (file list / verification step / named assumptions checked verbatim against push-back-on-the-plan.md l.15-38; 'you will notice the wait' l.16 of this lecture maps to that exercise's l.26 wait-guidance). Big Idea fidelity: this lecture's opening frame matches the module file's Big Idea ('Reading a plan is finite... Paired, they give a complete read; neither alone does') near word-for-word. Mood doesn't resolve early: the close stays in grounded-competence register ('the execution can wait for the day the task is real') without tipping into the felt payoff the exercise is about to deliver — it names the discipline, doesn't yet demonstrate having lived it.
